clue.text: Beds-the best part of the plan

parts.note: beds of rock are layers, also called strata
the gem of something is its finest part

explanation.surface: Someone says the beds are the finest feature of a home design.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ploy.

clue.text: Crests — the rocky expanses

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken up, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wave crests and rocky stretches of coastline make a seaside scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' shakes up the letters of CRESTS and THE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretches of land or water are wide areas, synonyms of expanses.

clue.text: Revive the mass-meeting

definitions.meaning: to recover strength, as a patient or market does
a big public gathering for a cause

explanation.definitionFit: To recover or pick up again is to rally, and a large political gathering is also called a rally.

clue.text: Picketed — what did I tell you with Teddy boy around?

indicators.note: around says the Teddy boy's short name goes round the other piece

parts.note: a Teddy boy is shortened to Ted, a 1950s British youth style
the exclamation 'There!' means 'told you so'

explanation.surface: A teased note about a 1950s youth hanging around a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, known as a Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: A picketed animal is tied to a stake, so it is tied up on a rope.

clue.text: Expression of surprise re a pleasure-seeker

parts.note: Gad! is an old exclamation of surprise
re means concerning, that is, about

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a hedonist.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is someone always out enjoying social pleasures.

clue.text: Power — to do it in would be aggressive

definitions.text: to do it in would be aggressive
definitions.meaning: the phrasal verb with 'in' means to push into a situation forcefully

explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means strength, and to push in pushily is to 'muscle in'.

clue.text: Calligraphic examples of dukes

definitions.meaning: a person's handwriting is called their fist
dukes is slang for hands or clenched hands, from rhyming slang

explanation.definitionFit: Samples of handwriting are fists in old slang, and 'put up your dukes' means raise your clenched hands.

clue.text: Duck, in fights, attacks

indicators.note: in puts the duck inside the fights

parts.note: frays are brawls or scuffles
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Someone dodges during brawls and raids.
explanation.definitionFit: Forays are sudden raids into enemy territory.

clue.text: Understands a flapper vacillating

parts.note: 'I see' means I understand
a wing is something that flaps

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper girl knows her own mind but keeps changing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesawing means swinging back and forth between choices, wavering.

clue.text: These positions said to be used by riflemen

indicators.note: said to be signals that the word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: sights are the aiming devices on a rifle

explanation.surface: A remark about firing positions on a shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are locations or places.

clue.text: Told to cheer, in a way

indicators.note: in puts the cheering verb inside the road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
to elate is to cheer up

explanation.surface: Someone was instructed to cheer in a particular manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Related a story means narrated or recounted it.

clue.text: A treacherous sort of present

indicators.note: sort of here means a variety or rearranged form of the following word

explanation.surface: A gift that turns out to be a betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and 'sort of' rearranges PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent in Eden is the archetype of treachery, and its letters are a reworking of a gift word.

clue.text: Herb's age, we hear

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is heard as another spelt differently

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone asks how old Herb is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a fragrant garden herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Jeers at confounded old clobber

parts.note: bally is old British slang meaning confounded or damned
clobber is British slang for clothes; old ones are rags

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a pile of wretched worn-out clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes, not a verb for hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ballyrag is to bully or scold someone, mocking them.

clue.text: Oddly enough she appears the country's Venus

indicators.note: oddly enough suggests something strange, so the short word is rearranged

parts.note: Peru's, a country, with the possessive giving an S

explanation.surface: Strangely, a goddess-like woman shows up as the beauty of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly enough' rearranges SHE into HES, then PERU'S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperus is the evening star, the planet Venus seen at dusk.

clue.text: The flow of learning

definitions.meaning: in schools, dividing pupils into ability groups

explanation.definitionFit: Streaming is a steady flowing, and in education it means grouping pupils by ability.

clue.text: Ducks-they may be lucky

definitions.meaning: a lucky dip is a fairground game of drawing a prize blind

explanation.definitionFit: Ducks under water are dips, and a lucky dip is a British grab-bag game.

clue.text: Yuletide night-watchers

parts.note: the Christmas story's flock-keepers who watched by night when the angel appeared

explanation.definitionFit: In the Nativity, flock-keepers watched their flocks by night.

clue.text: Used on nuts or by them in the works ?

definitions.text: Used on nuts or by them in the works ?

parts.words: Used on nuts or by them in the works ?
parts.note: a tool turns nuts and bolts; crazy people (nuts) throw one into the works to sabotage

explanation.definitionFit: Spanners tighten nuts, and 'a spanner in the works' is a British idiom for sabotage.

clue.text: Dim-—not like the crossword

definitions.meaning: a crossword has hints for every entry, so this lacks them

explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means dense, and literally means having no hints, unlike a puzzle.

clue.text: Like the head of Kipling's female when most deadly?

definitions.text: Like the head of Kipling's female when most deadly?

parts.words: Like the head of Kipling's female when most deadly?
parts.note: Kipling's poem shows the she-bear as deadlier than the male; a bear with a painful head is proverbially grumpy

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote 'The female of the species is more deadly than the male'; the she-bear is in it, and 'like a bear with a sore head' means very irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear in a temper is said to have an aching, painful head.

clue.text: Fable of a game in disorder

indicators.note: in puts the game inside the illness

parts.note: ague is a feverish illness, a disorder
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A tale of a sporting match in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologue is a moral tale or allegory.

clue.text: US rodent in the Ark? So we're told

definitions.text: in the Ark? So we're told
definitions.meaning: Genesis says the Ark was built of this wood

explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing American rodent shares its name with the wood Noah's Ark was made from in Genesis.

clue.text: The mouth of Leigh Hunt's Jenny

definitions.meaning: slang for the lips or face
in Leigh Hunt's poem 'Jenny kiss'd me', Jenny gave a kiss

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the mouth, and literally one who kisses, as Jenny did in Leigh Hunt's poem.

clue.text: Troubled one with no car-and that's very hard

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the pieces are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A distressed person without a vehicle finds things tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' jumbles I, NO, CAR and AND together.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian laws are excessively harsh and severe.

clue.text: Low-down on origin of some mugs

parts.note: the dope is the inside information

indicators.note: origin of means the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Inside information on where some coffee cups came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopes and mugs are both slang for fools.

clue.text: Four-cornered globe

parts.note: the biblical phrase speaks of the four corners of our world, though it is round

explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is round yet is said to have four corners.

clue.text: Early development of 24

indicators.note: development of means the letters are reworked into a new form

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, our planet

explanation.surface: An early stage of a project numbered 24.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old poetic word for early in the day or season.

clue.text: Conditions require soft illumination

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
lights give illumination

explanation.surface: Setting the mood needs gentle lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Plights are predicaments or bad states of affairs.

clue.text: He puts up, by direction, with the parson

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A host who takes in guests, guided by the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who builds or raises structures.

clue.text: Beat soundly with cane, yielding this

definitions.text: Beat soundly with cane, yielding this

parts.words: Beat soundly with cane, yielding this
parts.note: beat sounds like beet, which with cane are the two plants yielding the sweetener

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a caning; 'Beat soundly' means the vegetable beet, and beet and cane are the two crops refined into the sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: Both beet and cane are crops processed to make the sweet crystals.

clue.text: Die-hards on the subject of hospital workers

parts.note: re means concerning
in British hospitals a senior nurse is called a sister

explanation.surface: Stubborn people talking about the nurses on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Resisters are those who refuse to give in, like die-hards.
